source_text: In Dawoodi Bohra Ismaili doctrine, female genital cutting—termed khafd or khatna—constitutes an esoteric rite for achieving spiritual purity and chastity, with roots in Fatimid-era traditions as codified in the 10th-century jurisprudential text Da‘a’im al-Islam by Al-Qadi al-Nu’man, which emphasizes genital cutting for both sexes to foster moral discipline. [41]
